summary: Emigrant Butte lookout, Harney County, OR: house built 1921, 20-foot L-4 tower 1933, gone by the 1940s. No source describes the site today.

facts.design: Lookout house with cupola (1921); 20-foot L-4 tower (1933)
facts.status_note: Register and FireLookout.com say the tower was gone by the 1940s; no source describes remains

events.note: Ranger E.W. Donnelly built a lookout house (Central Oregonian, November 10, 1921); register dates a house with cupola to 1921
A new box-type house with glassed cupola for the fire finder (dated September 14, 1922); Thomas Ewing in charge that summer; register does not mention it
Al Frey, then Lester Williams for the rest of the season; Jack Choate from Dry Mountain in the autumn
20-foot L-4 tower replaced the house; W.H. Lohuis building the tower and house as one of several NRA projects
Forest Service request for approval of a combined garage, woodshed and storage building at the lookout (letter dated August 19, 1939)
Tower gone by the 1940s per register and FireLookout.com; exact year not given

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register and FireLookout.com date the first recorded house to 1921. Forest Lookouts records a 1921 house and a new house in September 1922 that the register does not mention. No source says whether the 1922 house replaced the 1921 one. Story reports both entries as written.

notes_for_editor: Read: the Former Fire Lookout Sites Register page, FireLookout.com, and Forest Lookouts' Oregon page with dated newspaper and Forest Service items from 1921 to 1939. Thin on the tower: no build contract, and the height and removal come from the register and FireLookout.com only, which may share a basis. No removal record found; the story gives only gone by the 1940s. The 1922 house is kept as written. Worth trying: Central Oregonian and Ochoconian issues 1933-1945, Ochoco National Forest records, and the Harney County Historical Society. The 2008 photo credit (Ron Kemnow) is the nominator's for the register and was not followed up.
